episode.title: Rank structured PreToolUse permission decisions by restrictiveness
episode.before: When multiple matching PreToolUse hooks produced hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision values, the aggregator treated permissionDecision and permissionDecisionReason as ordinary last-wins fields. A later configuration-order allow or ask could replace an earlier deny, and the downstream PreToolUse accessor consumed that overwritten hook-specific value, so the deny did not block the tool. The issue report described this as completion-order nondeterminism, but the repository call path shows deterministic input/configuration-order overwrite because parallel results are returned by Promise.all in input order.
episode.after: For multiple PreToolUse outputs, the aggregator selects the most restrictive structured permission decision using deny > ask > allow, independent of input or configuration order. It retains permissionDecisionReason values only from the winning rank and joins equal-rank reasons in merge order. Single-output behavior, top-level decision OR logic, additionalContext and artifact aggregation, and last-wins behavior for unrelated hook-specific fields remain unchanged.
episode.diff: Commit c9a9a8ad147744085487738f51e1618057c9baa5 changes packages/core/src/hooks/hookAggregator.ts by adding a permission-decision rank table, tracking the winning PreToolUse decision and its same-rank reasons, excluding permissionDecision and permissionDecisionReason from generic last-wins copying, and emitting the ranked result. It changes the mergeWithOrLogic call path to receive the event name so the special handling is limited to PreToolUse. It adds eight focused regression tests covering deny/allow order independence, deny/ask, ask/allow, winning and same-rank reasons, single-hook behavior, preservation of unrelated-field last-wins behavior, and outputs without a permission decision.

evidence_units.claim: The implementation commit changes only the hook aggregator and its collocated unit test: packages/core/src/hooks/hookAggregator.ts has 52 insertions and 1 deletion, and packages/core/src/hooks/hookAggregator.test.ts has 138 insertions.

Issue #12683 is closed as completed, and the GitHub bundle records the linked merged PR #12689 as the resolution. The linked PR describes the intended contract as deny > ask > allow for hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision while preserving unrelated merge semantics.
evidence_units.source: issue-bundle.json: issue.state/state_reason/closed_at; timeline cross-reference to PR #12689; linked PR #12689 body

evidence_units.claim: Before the fix, mergeOutputs returned a single output unchanged, but multiple PreToolUse outputs were routed through mergeWithOrLogic. Its hookSpecificOutput loop copied every field except additionalContext and artifacts into a generic accumulator, so later permissionDecision and permissionDecisionReason values overwrote earlier values.

Before the fix, top-level decision already used block/deny OR logic, but permissionDecision was not handled separately. A top-level block therefore could coexist with a conflicting hookSpecificOutput allow, and the PreToolUse accessor preferred the hook-specific value.

The fixed aggregator defines allow=1, ask=2, and deny=3, tracks the highest-ranked PreToolUse permission decision, clears previously collected lower-rank reasons when a higher rank appears, and appends non-empty reasons when the rank ties.

The fixed generic hook-specific merge skips permissionDecision and permissionDecisionReason only for PreToolUse, then emits the selected decision and joined winning-rank reasons while continuing generic handling for other event types and unrelated fields.

The PreToolUse event handler executes matching hooks, aggregates their results, and returns the aggregate. The public PreToolUse event wrapper returns finalOutput, making the repaired aggregate the value passed to downstream consumers.

The downstream PreToolUse gate creates a PreToolUseHookOutput from the returned output, calls isDenied or isAsk, and uses getPermissionDecisionReason for the block result. getPermissionDecision reads hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision before falling back to the top-level decision.

Parallel hook execution maps the configuration array and returns Promise.all(promises), which preserves result-array input order regardless of completion timing. The event handler constructs that array as registry hook configurations followed by session hook configurations, supporting the triage correction that the old overwrite was deterministic configuration-order behavior rather than completion-order aggregation.
evidence_units.source: packages/core/src/hooks/hookRunner.ts at c9a9a8ad147744085487738f51e1618057c9baa5:982-1010; packages/core/src/hooks/hookEventHandler.ts at c9a9a8ad147744085487738f51e1618057c9baa5:985-1002; issue-bundle.json: triage comment on issue #12683

evidence_units.claim: The added tests aggregate multiple PreToolUse outputs and assert deny wins over allow in both input orders, deny wins over ask, and ask wins over allow through the PreToolUseHookOutput accessors.

The added tests assert that reasons come from the winning rank and concatenate for equal ranks, that a single hook remains unchanged, that updatedInput keeps last-wins behavior, and that an output containing only additionalContext cannot lower an existing deny.

The collocated unit tests directly exercise aggregateResults for the structured PreToolUse contract and provide an oracle for severity precedence, order independence, reason propagation, single-output compatibility, and unrelated-field compatibility.

candidate_atomics.name: rank_pretool_permission_verdict
candidate_atomics.description: Make the structured permission verdict from multiple matching PreToolUse hooks severity-aware so aggregation cannot weaken a restrictive result because of input or configuration order; retain reason information only from the winning rank, joining equal-rank reasons.

semantic_action.intent: Preserve the strongest safety-relevant permission outcome when multiple structured hook results contribute to one tool-execution gate.
semantic_action.pre_state: Multiple matching hook outputs contribute hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision values, but generic last-wins merging lets a later allow or ask replace an earlier deny; the downstream PreToolUse gate consumes the merged hook-specific value.
semantic_action.post_state: The aggregate contains the most restrictive supplied structured permission decision under deny > ask > allow, independent of input order, and exposes only the corresponding winning-rank reason(s), with equal-rank reasons joined in merge order.
semantic_action.validation: Focused aggregateResults tests assert deny dominates allow in both orders, deny dominates ask, ask dominates allow, and the resulting PreToolUse accessors report the expected blocking or confirmation state.
parameters: ordered collection of matching hook outputs

candidate_atomics.name: assert_ranked_permission_aggregation_contract
candidate_atomics.description: Add a focused regression oracle for the structured permission aggregation contract and its compatibility boundary.

semantic_action.intent: Make the restrictive multi-hook permission contract executable as a regression check.
semantic_action.pre_state: The generic merge behavior had no direct tests for multiple hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision values, so an overwritten deny could pass existing tests.
semantic_action.post_state: The collocated test suite specifies severity precedence, input-order independence, winning-rank reason behavior, single-hook behavior, preservation of unrelated last-wins fields, and no-decision outputs.
semantic_action.validation: The focused hook aggregator tests are the direct oracle: they construct aggregateResults inputs and assert the final PreToolUse decision, reason, and unrelated-field values.
parameters: ordered test sequences of hook outputs

candidate_workflows.name: repair_structured_permission_aggregation_contract
candidate_workflows.description: Repair the multi-source structured permission contract at the aggregation boundary and then validate the restrictive ordering and compatibility boundary for other hook output fields.

workflow_graph.goal: Ensure all matching PreToolUse hooks jointly determine a deterministic, non-weakenable permission outcome before tool execution.
workflow_graph.entry_state: The aggregation path receives multiple matching hook outputs, but the structured permission verdict is treated as an ordinary last-wins field and can be weakened by a later allow or ask.
workflow_graph.exit_state: The final PreToolUse output reports deny > ask > allow regardless of input or configuration order, carries the winning-rank reason policy, and leaves unrelated aggregation contracts intact with regression coverage.
unresolved_or_deferred: The reporter described completion-order nondeterminism, but the issue-bundle triage and Promise.all/configuration code establish deterministic input/configuration-order last-wins behavior; the implementation addresses the severity contract rather than a scheduler race.
The reported parallel-tool-batch hang was explicitly not reproduced and is outside this episode.
The pinned commit's validation is unit-level; no new end-to-end CLI or tool execution is part of the checkout diff.
The implementation intentionally leaves top-level decision OR logic separate from hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision ranking.

unresolved_questions: The focused test command was not independently completed in this environment: npx Vitest failed because the native Rolldown binding was unavailable, and the Corepack pnpm invocation failed signature verification. The committed tests remain direct validation evidence, but their execution here is unverified.

The pinned implementation does not fold top-level decision values into the new permissionDecision rank. Mixed outputs using both decision spellings therefore retain the pre-existing separate semantics; the linked PR explicitly describes top-level decision aggregation as unchanged.
The related parallel-tool-batch hang in the issue report was not reproduced and is not established as part of this fix.
Pattern induction across multiple repositories and leakage-audited holdout validation are outside this single-episode extraction.
